newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Perio suspends U.S. share offer.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Perio suspends U.S. share offer.

text.p: Israel's Perio Products Ltd said on Thursday it had suspended its U.S. share offering due next week until it could get U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for its main product.

A spokesman for the company, a subsidiary of Israel Chemicals, said officials believed Perio would go public at a higher valuation after the FDA approved the Perio chip, a product designed to fight gum disease.
"They decided to postpone the offering because they still don't have FDA approval and because with approval they can get a much higher price," said a spokeswoman for Israel Chemicals.
Perio expected to raise $35 million in an offering for 20 percent of equity.
A source close to the company indciated that Perio had believed it would get the FDA go-ahead prior to the originally planned offering.
Israel Chemicals' share price fell 3.75 percent in trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange and analysts attributed the fall to the announcement.
"It's a very, very strange announcement. They knew a long time ago that if they got FDA approval the price would be higher," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.
The spokeswoman said the FDA approval could take weeks or months but that the company is confident its product would be approved.
Underwriters included Smith Barney, Salomon Brothers, Oppenheimer & Co and the Israeli brokerage IBI.
The Perio chip is a gum implant which releases an anti-infectious substance.
